overall: The AG found the Dartmouth Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law on all four alleged points at its February 13, 2023 meeting, and ordered immediate and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Board did not state the purpose of the executive session in open session at its February 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board failed to announce the name of the member who participated remotely at the February 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Board admits, and we agree, that the Chair did not announce in open session the purpose for the executive session and failed to announce the name of the one member who was participating remotely during the February 13 meeting.

allegations.summary: Board took open-session votes by voice rather than roll call while a member participated remotely at the February 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because one member of the Board participated remotely during the February 13 meeting, all votes taken during that meeting must be by roll call vote, even unanimous votes.

allegations.summary: Chair did not announce at the start of the February 13 meeting that it was being recorded and broadcast.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Chair did not make such an announcement, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
